about: The Glaza statement (#109; scope-v1 module 13; question #580; decision 0265). For a club month of Glaza's lines: the food, soft drinks and alcohol RIVR comped are owed to Glaza at cost; the margin on alcohol sold (price less cost) is split 50:50, RIVR's half the margin divided by two and rounded toward nothing to the paisa, so Glaza keeps an odd paisa; NewCo's payable to Glaza is the comps less RIVR's half, below nothing when Glaza owes RIVR. Inputs are the comps at cost and the alcohol margin; expected is RIVR's share and the payable.

cases.description: A month of comps and alcohol: half the margin comes off the comps.
An odd paisa of margin stays with Glaza.
Three paise of margin: RIVR takes one, Glaza two.
No comps and no alcohol: nothing either way.
Half the margin equal to the comps: nothing either way.
More alcohol margin than comps: Glaza owes RIVR.
Alcohol sold below cost: RIVR bears half the loss.
Three paise below cost: RIVR bears one, Glaza two.
